newsitem.title: USA: US Plains feedlot cattle quiet, no sales - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains feedlot cattle quiet, no sales - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet early Monday, with no reported sales, feedlot sources said.
Packer bids were light at $63.00 per cwt and being passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00 to $66.00. Prices this week were seen steady to $1.00 higher, compared with last week's top of $64.00.

Feedlots remained current following last week's heavy volume. Sales last week were estimated at 137,000 head in the Texas Panhandle/western Oklahoma areas and 118,000 in Kansas, according to the feedlot sources.
Some sources said meat packers used Friday's bearish USDA Cattle-on-Feed report to bid lower for cattle Monday at $63.00.

The USDA report showed January placements at 125 percent of a year ago, which greatly exceeded trade estimates. CME April live cattle futures were called to open 0.50 cent per lb lower Tuesday and 1.00 cent lower in June and August.
This week's showlists were seen unchanged to slightly smaller than this week's, cattlemen said.
A survey of major U.S. beef packers indicate most will be operating Monday during the U.S. Presidents Day holiday.
